test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following methods can be used to conserve our natural resources?

options.text: Turning on lights even when not required
Walking to nearby places without using vehicles

solution:
The correct answer is __**Walking to nearby places without using vehicles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural resources **are materials and components that occur naturally in the environment and can be used for economic gain or to meet human needs. 
 
• They are typically classified into two main categories:** renewable and non-renewable resources.**
 
• **Renewable Resources** are those resources that can be replenished naturally over time.
 
• **Non-renewable resources** are those Resources that do not replenish at a sustainable rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance of Natural Resources**

 
 
• **Economic Development:** Natural resources are crucial for industries and agriculture, driving economic growth.
 
• **Energy Production**: Many resources provide energy necessary for modern life, from electricity to transportation.
 
• **Ecosystem Services**: They support ecosystems that provide clean air, water, and biodiversity, which are essential for life.
 
• **Raw Materials: **Used in manufacturing and construction, contributing to infrastructure and technological advancement.
 
 
 
• **Challenges and Issues**
 
 
• **Overexploitation**: Unsustainable use of resources can lead to depletion, habitat destruction, and biodiversity loss.
 
• **Pollution**: Extraction and use of natural resources can lead to air, water, and soil pollution.
 
• **Climate Change**: Fossil fuel consumption significantly contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, affecting global temperatures and weather patterns.
 
• **Resource Conflicts**: Competition for limited resources can lead to social and political tensions, especially in areas with scarce water or arable land.
